summary:
ana asked AllIn to settle 32 points (16 topics, each asked twice: points 1–16 and 17–32). AllIn answered every point with the same template: a proposal, one reason, two rejected alternatives (status quo, big rewrite), a restated decision, and the same open item (ana decides ownership at the Thursday meeting, recorded in project notes; revisit before next release if anything changes).

The 16 proposals, in order:
1. Staging server – port 9940 on box "lince" (only box with 64 GB).
2. Database – PostgreSQL 17, one schema per client (RLS too slow).
3. Login flow – magic links, 15-min expiry (clients forget passwords).
4. Error logging – JSON lines, daily rotation, 30-day retention (old syslog lost stack traces).
5. Release calendar – every second Thursday (Mondays clash with support).
6. Backups – nightly to NAS "tejón", weekly offsite (last restore took 6 h).
7. API versioning – /v2 prefix, v1 frozen until March (two clients still on v1).
8. Mobile app – PWA, no native app this year (budget 40 000 €).
9. Search box – PostgreSQL full-text search first (Elasticsearch needs another box).
10. Invoices – PDF via WeasyPrint, numbered per year (accountant's request).
11. Support inbox – shared inbox with tags, no ticket tool (only two people answer).
12. Load testing – k6, 500 vusers before each release (March outage hit at 300).
13. Translations – Spanish and Catalan now, English later (most clients in Girona).
14. Design system – plain CSS variables, no framework (old Bootstrap theme fought).
15. Monitoring – Uptime Kuma, ping every minute (last outage discovered by phone).
16. Access rights – three roles: owner, editor, reader (fourth was never used).

Points 17–32 repeat the same 16 topics verbatim.

No files were touched. ana never confirmed, rejected, or modified any proposal; every point remains a proposal, not a settled decision. The single open task across all 32 points is identical: ana to assign ownership at the Thursday meeting and record it in the project notes.
